text.p: These are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Friday. Prepared for Reuters by the Co-operation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Standard & Poor's credit rating for Latvia, announced on Thursday, is of investment grade. It is BBB for long-term foreign currency credits, A-3 for short-term issue and A-2 for short-term issue in lats.
- Parliament approved Vassili Melnik of the Democratic Party Saimnieks as the new Finance Minister by 44 votes against 24.
- Transport Minister Vilis Krishtopans has not approved Andrej Inkulis, mayor of Jurmala, as the Riga port manager, saying he lacks qualifications for the job.

- Russia wants to participate in a joint venture in Liepaja harbour, the biggest former Soviet naval base on the Baltic sea, says Arkadii Volsky, chairman of the Association of Russia's Industrialists. Volsky denied earlier reports that quoted him as saying that Russia wants to buy the base. A development project shows the harbour needs at least $20 million in investment, said Volski.
- Former prime minister Maris Gailis plans to publish his memoirs about the six years he spent in the government.
- Parex Bank has received permission from the central bank to open branches in Karaganda (Kazakhstan), Bishkek and offices in Alma-Ata (Kazakhstan) and Geneva.
- The Riga Customs Board has confiscated a large cargo of narcotic drugs from Russia, arrested this week.
- Rietumu banka reports last year's profit of 4.3 million lats.
- The cabinet has changed rules on transit visas, allowing private visas to be issued to persons who accompany or receive shipments or deliver them to ports and airports.
